column1: # Recorded release inventory for the REQ-SYSTEST-002 producer gate.
# The shapes here are the ones the real pulseengine releases have — recorded,
# not invented — so the layer-assembly path is driven by realistic metadata
# without reaching GitHub. The gate must not depend on the network, nor on
# somebody's release still existing at the version this file names.
# SCOPE (REQ-SYSTEST-001 clause 3 — a fixture states what it cannot prove):
# the ASSET BYTES are small stand-ins, not the real binaries, so this fixture
# proves nothing about what the shipped tools do. What it does exercise is
# everything the assembler itself decides: which assets are selected for which
# platform, that each is checksummed against its own release's VERIFIED sums,
# that a repo named twice is downloaded once and a repo named at two versions
# is refused, and that the resulting spec is one `varve deposit` accepts.
#   tar:<binary>:flat    a .tar.gz holding <binary> at the root
#   tar:none             a .tar.gz holding no binary at all
#   raw                  a bare downloadable file (sigil's wsc binaries)
# `!sums-style` sets how a repo writes SHA256SUMS.txt. Both forms are real and
# both must parse — hence the `[ /]` in the assembler's grep and the `s# \./# #`
# rivet — appears in BOTH lists: a CLI and a VS Code extension from one
# release. This is the pair that killed the 2026.08.3 deposit.
# A SECOND rivet release, complete and downloadable. The version-skew scenario
# must be refused by the assembler's guard and NOT by the fixture running out
# of assets — a test that passes because the wrong thing was missing is not a
# spar — also in both lists, and its extension is PER PLATFORM: four packages,
# each of which must land with its own varve `platform` so a consumer resolves
# loom — ships NO aarch64-apple-darwin tarball. That is a notice and an
# omission from the layer, never a failed deposit.
# kiln — the tool is `kiln`, the binary inside is `kilnd`. The `:binary`
# field of a TARBALL_TOOLS entry is what makes that work.
# sigil — raw per-platform binaries, named sigil's way rather than by triple.
# hollow — a release whose tarballs carry no binary of the declared name, the
# shape an upstream layout change produces. Used only by the negative case.
